target_customer: Developers, storage providers and token holders in decentralized web and storage networks
problem: HTTP location addressing is fragile and centralized. IPFS uses content addressing, and Filecoin pays storage providers in tokens.
business_model: Open source protocols funded by token sales, plus investment arms (PL R&D, PL Capital)

founders.name: Juan Benet
founders.background_notes: YC page says he founded Protocol Labs, IPFS and Filecoin. Wikipedia says founded May 2014, IPFS released January 2015.

technical_complexity.rationale: Designing a global content addressed peer to peer file system and later proof of storage consensus is research grade work.

defensibility.rationale: Open source protocols with a growing developer and provider network, though open source limits exclusivity.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Wikipedia style coverage frames IPFS against HTTP, BitTorrent and Freenet; none absorbed it.

market_need_then: Interest in decentralized web and censorship resistant storage, then the 2017 token sale raised a record amount, evidencing demand.

branding.domain_note: protocol.ai redirects to pl.xyz as of 2026.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission language about computing breakthroughs for humanity.

branding.brand_signature: IPFS and Filecoin as flagship project brands, with trademarks registered by the company
branding.community_and_virality: IPFS is widely used by developers; PL cites about 3,000 active contributors and 750 network members (company claim).

brand_strength.rationale: Project brands IPFS and Filecoin are better known than the parent name; evidence is the company's own claims and trademark records.

outcome_analysis: Protocol Labs turned the IPFS research project into a large network company, funding Filecoin with a record 2017 token sale of roughly 257 million dollars. It cut 21 percent of staff (89 roles) in February 2023 during the crypto downturn, showing sensitivity to crypto cycles, but remains active with a team of about 130 per YC.
notes: Token sale amounts: CoinDesk says about 52M presale and about 205.8M public sale, 257M combined; the sale is not a classic equity round so stage is other. Pre-YC or later venture equity rounds not searched beyond this. Competitor sources found were undated Wikipedia mirrors so the list is empty. Team size 130 per YC versus layoffs in 2023. Audit additions: the 2014 YC investment of about 120K rests on one outlet, a Halcyonic (System Explorers) Substack post that says Benet received 120,000 dollars from Y Combinator; no YC page or second source gives the amount, and the YC S14 batch is confirmed separately. The 2016-03 round of about 3M is reported by Startupintros (announced 2016-03-01, stage labelled Series U, amount only) and a Village snippet (dated 2016-03-24) naming Haystack, FundersClub, Digital Currency Group, Techammer, DHVC and Boost VC; the investor names rest on the Village aggregator alone (page returned 403, snippet only) and the full Startupintros investor list is a lump of all later investors, so it is not used. CB Insights shows a separate 2016-05-23 seed of unknown size and a total of 4.73M, which conflicts and is not recorded.
